items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: I was listening to a lot of Dixieland as well, some Louis Armstrong, Jack Teagarden, and Miff Mole and his Little Molars.

ctx.x: And so I was listening to Charlie Parker and Coleman Hawkins, Lester, and Basie and everybody, when I was just a little kid. Because there was no T.V. at the time when I was growing up, and so on rainy days before I went to kindergarten, my parents would just sit me in front of the — well my mother would sit me in front of the record player and just let me go. And I was listening to a lot of Dixieland as well, some Louis Armstrong, Jack Teagarden, and Miff Mole and his Little Molars. Remember them? So it was a…

stuff being played. But record stores — to a degree, to a degree. Probably a better selection of jazz record stores than we have now in the States, but I used to buy directly from the States. I had a subscription to “DownBeat” magazine and I’d read all these things, and I’d also get “Voice of America” on shortwave radio. And so I would hear all these great things like Art Blakey, Horace Silver, Max Roach, all these wonderful players. And the guy would say, “and this is from their latest album,” bang. So I would…
